- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert — reduce forecast peak by 5-10% and slow downward slope.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.20), model underestimates upward momentum — increase forecast by 2-5% for next 3-5 days.  
- When sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model often lags — delay peak forecast by 1-2 days and raise slope gently.  
- If model consistently underpredicts true price in early days of forecast horizon (e.g., day 1-3), add 1-2% to forecast to account for lagged sentiment impact.  
- If sentiment is volatile or erratic, reduce forecast volatility — smooth out sharp swings by 1-2% per day.
